daily.title: Trump threatens to block Canada's Bombardier planes from US market
daily.summary: Trump says Bombardier must build aircraft in the US as Canada imposes tariffs of up to 50% on US imports.

daily.title: Ukraine updates: Explosions rock Kyiv as 3-day truce ends
daily.summary: A series of explosions rocked Kyiv and neighboring cities signaling the end of Russia's three-day ceasefire. DW has the latest.

daily.title: Eiffel Tower employees strike after female staff removed
daily.summary: The employees protested against the removal of the site's female workers due to a request by a visiting Hindu group. The tower's operating company apologized for the decision.

daily.title: 3 years on, Morocco earthquake victims still wait for help
daily.summary: Reconstruction has progressed in the three years since the 2023 Morocco earthquake, but some survivors are still living in tents. Locals are divided as to how successful it's been, and whether state aid is enough.

daily.title: Werner Herzog: Germany's wild man of cinema is back
daily.summary: As his latest movie, "Bucking Fastard," premiered at the Venice Film Festival, DW talked to the boundary-breaking director.

daily.title: Nicaragua challenges German arms exports to Israel at ICJ
daily.summary: Germany has asked the International Court of Justice to dismiss the case on jurisdiction grounds. It also said its arms exports to Israel were documented, published, and subject to more stringent checks than most.

daily.title: Saxony-Anhalt: Germany wakes up to 'unsettling' AfD victory
daily.summary: The far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) party won the Saxony-Anhalt state election but without an absolute majority in parliament. Other European nations were wrestling with the impact of the results. Follow DW.

daily.title: Can the AfD form a government in Saxony-Anhalt?
daily.summary: Following its record election success, the far-right Alternative for Germany aims to form a government. What options does it have without the absolute majority?

daily.title: Russia announces it is closing Germany's consulate in St. Petersburg
daily.summary: The tit-for-tat reaction comes after Germany said it is shutting down Russia's consulate in Bonn and its cultural center in Berlin.

daily.title: War criminal Ratko Mladic buried with military honors in Belgrade, Serbia
daily.summary: Ratko Mladic, the former Bosnian Serb commander convicted of genocide in Srebrenica, has been buried in Belgrade. The funeral, broadcast live on TV, comes just days before President Vucic is expected to call an election.

daily.title: Chancellor Merz says AfD result 'changes all of Germany'
daily.summary: A visibly shaken but also determined Friedrich Merz spoke in Berlin about the AfD's election victory in Saxony-Anhalt and the CDU's bitter defeat. He insisted on sticking to his reforms.

daily.title: Carbon capture tech exists. Scaling it up is the hard part
daily.summary: Europe just opened a carbon capture and storage plant billed as the continent's largest. But global climate scenarios call for far more capacity than exists anywhere on Earth.

daily.title: Pakistan: Can creating new provinces fix governance?
daily.summary: Pakistanis broadly agree that the country needs more responsive and effective government, but many question whether simply creating more provinces is the solution.

daily.title: EU's von der Leyen pledges $232 million Greenland investment
daily.summary: The EU is preparing a major investment package and closer political ties with the Danish Arctic territory amid Donald Trump's demand for greater US control of the mineral-rich island.

daily.title: Threatening letters revive fears among Kashmiri Pandits
daily.summary: Leaked addresses and phone numbers have reignited fears among Hindu government employees who returned to Muslim-majority Kashmir under a rehabilitation scheme.

daily.title: Russia opens first road bridge with North Korea
daily.summary: Russia and North Korea have opened their first road bridge across the Tumen River as political, economic and military ties between the two countries deepen.

daily.title: Middle East: Israeli strikes kill a dozen in Lebanon
daily.summary: Lebanon's Health Ministry said at least 12 were killed in overnight Israeli strikes in the south of the country. Meanwhile, traffic in the Strait of Hormuz has sunk to its lowest level since May.

daily.title: Ukraine: Zelenskyy says war looks set to go on into winter
daily.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy says there appears to be no end in sight in Russia's war against his country. His words come after another round of US-led diplomacy. DW has the latest.

daily.title: UK government condemns 'thuggish' anti-migrant protests in Portsmouth
daily.summary: Hundreds gathered in Portsmouth after some refugees arrived by boat from France, a day after masked protesters disrupted traffic at the port of Dover.

daily.title: India news: Rescue efforts underway in deadly Delhi building collapse
daily.summary: The building was located in New Delhi's Satya Niketan, popular among students from nearby colleges and universities. At least 12 people have been rescued from the rubble.

weekly.title: US envoys Witkoff and Kushner hold Ukraine talks after meeting Putin
weekly.summary: US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner held talks with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy in Kyiv, seeking to revive efforts to end the war. But the latest diplomatic push seems to have produced no breakthrough.

weekly.title: Saxony-Anhalt: Digesting the AfD's landmark election win
weekly.summary: With well over 40% for the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD), Saxony-Anhalt has witnessed a landmark election night. DW's reporters were on the ground.

weekly.title: Fact check: Election fraud claims spread in Saxony-Anhalt
weekly.summary: False and misleading claims are raising questions about the integrity of the election in Saxony-Anhalt. DW Fact Check takes a closer look.

weekly.title: Germany set to feel the impact of Saxony-Anhalt's AfD win
weekly.summary: The state election could have major consequences for Germany's government. Pollsters cite dissatisfaction with Merz as one reason for the CDU's poor showing.

weekly.title: Saxony-Anhalt election: Why the AfD is so strong
weekly.summary: The AfD has emerged as the strongest party in Germany's eastern state of Saxony-Anhalt by a wide margin. What is driving support for the far right in this predominantly rural eastern German state?

weekly.title: Germany, Kosovo unite against ticks carrying deadly virus
weekly.summary: Germany has high-security labs while Kosovo has Hyalomma ticks and experience with the deadly Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever. Working together, German and Kosovar scientists are fighting the disease and its vectors.

weekly.title: Germany plans anti-drone shield over Leipzig attack — report
weekly.summary: Several German cities will receive rapidly deployable units capable of defending against drone strikes on critical infrastructure, according to Bild am Sonntag newspaper.

weekly.title: Hungary begins hunt for corrupt regime's billions
weekly.summary: Hungary's new prime minister promised he would recover billions stolen or diverted by the previous administration. A new "super authority" is about to begin that work. Its success or failure will have a big impact.

weekly.title: Croatia: Toxic waste protest draws tens of thousands
weekly.summary: The Zagreb demonstrators demanded that the government come up with a plan to clear illegal toxic waste in 20 days. Prime Minister Plenkovic has promised to tackle the issue.

weekly.title: Germany: From emigration to immigration destination
weekly.summary: Migration is a sensitive topic in Germany, with public debate dominated by the fear of uncontrolled immigration. But over two centuries, millions of Germans emigrated in search of a better life.

weekly.title: Germany news: Thousands march at Saxony-Anhalt rallies
weekly.summary: Ahead of Saxony-Anhalt's state election on Sunday, a democracy festival by civil society groups has been held in Magdeburg. The far-right AfD organized its final campaign rally in the state capital.

weekly.title: What would an AfD government in Saxony-Anhalt really mean?
weekly.summary: Detention centers for deportation, mandatory work for asylum-seekers, vigilante groups — the AfD wants to drastically overhaul Saxony-Anhalt. What does the party have planned?

weekly.title: Outrage as Maltese tycoon acquitted in journalist's murder
weekly.summary: Maltese businessman Yorgen Fenech has been found not guilty of complicity to murder journalist Daphne Caruana Galizia. Almost nine years after the attack, the question of who ordered her death remains unanswered.

weekly.title: In Saxony-Anhalt election, small parties will be kingmakers
weekly.summary: The far-right AfD has good odds of winning an absolute majority in Saxony-Anhalt's parliament this state election, enabling them to govern alone. It all depends on whether other parties make the cut.

weekly.title: Germany's civil society alliance takes on the far right
weekly.summary: Trade unions, churches and human rights activists are worried about the rise of the far-right AfD. How can civil society protect people who are threatened by far-right extremism?

weekly.title: How vulnerable is Germany's infrastructure?
weekly.summary: The growing number of attacks on substations and railway lines in Germany is raising concern. Experts say that people will have to get used to the likelihood that such incidents will continue.

weekly.title: Majority of Germans see Russia as a threat
weekly.summary: More than half of German citizens believe that Germany's security is threatened by Russia, according to the latest survey by public broadcaster ARD.

weekly.title: The hidden environmental cost of AI data centers
weekly.summary: As data centers multiply to meet AI demand, they're straining power grids, draining water supplies and reshaping the land and air around them.

weekly.title: Serbia: How the funeral of Ratko Mladic is dividing a nation
weekly.summary: As the Serbian government leaves the decision about Ratko Mladic's funeral arrangements to his family, international pressure on the country is mounting. How do Serbs feel about the matter?

weekly.title: Germany: Is Saxony-Anhalt's economy really struggling?
weekly.summary: Germany's far-right AfD party has long claimed that the eastern state of Saxony-Anhalt has been left behind. Is that really the case? A closer look at the data offers some interesting insights.

weekly.title: Why North Korea's women's football team is so good
weekly.summary: North Korea's young footballers enter the U-20 World Cup in Poland as defending champions — the 2024 title was their third. Why is the isolated state so good at the game?

weekly.title: 2026 Beethoven Festival evokes a sense of home
weekly.summary: The motto of this year's classical music festival in Bonn is "Home/At Home," featuring musicians from diverse cultures presenting pieces from their homelands.

weekly.title: How Volkswagen's huge workforce became a costly burden
weekly.summary: The struggling German carmaker plans to cut up to 100,000 jobs from its 630,000-strong workforce. How did VW's headcount get so bloated, and will the cuts be enough to survive the Chinese EV onslaught?

weekly.title: Berlin: BER Airport Terminal 1 reopened after security scare
weekly.summary: Police have given the all-clear at Terminal 1 at Berlin's BER Airport following an earlier security scare and evacuation. The airport said some flights had been delayed but they were trying to avoid any cancelations.

weekly.title: Norway seizes Russian ship in Svalbard to compensate Ukraine
weekly.summary: Authorities in Norway have seized a Russian ship, the Professor Molchanov, on a court order sought and obtained by Naftogaz in Ukraine. Russia has protested the move, which stems from its refusal to pay Naftogaz damages.

weekly.title: Is Germany's economic slump finally over?
weekly.summary: Despite a slew of negative headlines, the German economy has posted its best figures in years. There are reasons for optimism, but structural issues remain.

weekly.title: Germany news: Police say arson attack targeted defense firm
weekly.summary: Two people were arrested in connection with a small fire at a construction site near a defense tech company in Munich. Investigators are looking at a possible "political motive."

weekly.title: Russia to close branches of Germany's Goethe-Institut
weekly.summary: Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov said the move was in response to Germany's decision to close the Russian House in Berlin after blaming Moscow for an attempted drone attack at Leipzig/Halle Airport.

weekly.title: Germany: How to woo voters with an immigrant background
weekly.summary: The number of voters in Germany with an immigrant background is rising. Yet the established parties barely manage to reach them. Why not?

weekly.title: Macron visits Bayeux Tapestry with King Charles, PM Andy Burnham
weekly.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron is on a shorter-term visit to the UK than the renowned on-loan 11th century tapestry. He viewed the ancient artwork with the UK monarch and relatively new Prime Minister Andy Burnham.

weekly.title: Russia's hybrid attacks on Germany: how should Berlin react?
weekly.summary: Germany holds Russia responsible for an attempted drone attack on Leipzig airport. But critics say Berlin's response, including the closure of Russia's consulate in Bonn, has been too timid.

weekly.title: Austria women ice hockey team fight for future generations
weekly.summary: Austria are getting ready for their first Women's Ice Hockey World Championship. But preparations have been overshadowed by a dispute about conditions, pay and getting men's cast-off kit. A solution now looks in sight.

weekly.title: EU summons Russian envoy over failed Leipzig drone attack
weekly.summary: The EU's foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas said the attempted attack had "all the hallmarks of state-sponsored terrorism." She said the EU was summoning a Russian envoy, with France announcing a similar step.

weekly.title: Women's football: Anyomi, London City and the German exodus
weekly.summary: Nicole Anyomi has joined Alexia Putellas and other star names in signing for the ambitious English club London City Lionesses. The Germany winger told DW England is a better place to develop her game than back home.

weekly.title: Ukraine: Russia threatens 'devastating' Baltic response
weekly.summary: Any escalation in the Baltic region will lead to a significant response, Moscow said.

weekly.title: Germany says Russia behind attempted drone attack at Leipzig airport
weekly.summary: Investigators believe an explosives-laden drone was deliberately targeting a Ukrainian cargo aircraft at Leipzig/Halle airport in early August. The German government said on Tuesday that it held Russia "responsible."

weekly.title: Can communities be proteced from melting glaciers?
weekly.summary: Rising temperatures are increasing the risk of floods and avalanches in mountain regions. The disaster in Nepal and Tibet shows the urgent need for solutions, and the tools that could help save lives.

weekly.title: Mladic's death, Bosnia and Serbia's unfinished reckoning
weekly.summary: The death of Ratko Mladic did not close a dark chapter of European history; it reopened old wounds. The ideology that created him lives on. The Dayton peace agreement ended the war, not the divisions that produced it.

weekly.title: Norway's new King Haakon VIII takes oath in parliament
weekly.summary: The new king swore to uphold the constitution in parliament in Oslo, the first major institutional step of his reign. Haakon VIII's wife Queen Mette-Marit had to skip the event in the aftermath of her lung transplant.

weekly.title: US irks Germany, Europe with Russian G20 invite, press bans
weekly.summary: Russia's finance minister is at the G20 meeting in Asheville but some key US press corps members are not. The mood was already tense amid the lengthy Iran war and Trump's renewed beef with neighbor Canada.

weekly.title: Can new Apple CEO John Ternus fix the tech giant's AI woes?
weekly.summary: John Ternus is just the third Apple CEO in 30 years. His primary challenge is to correct the company's faltering AI strategy to preserve its position as a big tech leader.
